A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PromptHMR paper, with 15 readable pages including references and supplementary Sections 7–8. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–15 are identical; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments and prompt ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–5, and supplementary Section 7.1/Figure 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 1–5, and supplementary Section 7.1/Figure 9.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same image encoder, spatial and semantic prompting, SMPL-X decoder, interaction attention, temporal extension, and training losses.

E1.justification: Training datasets and task coverage remain identical. Both evaluate reconstruction, interactions, body shape, and video motion using the same 3DPW, EMDB, RICH, HI4D, CHI3D, and HBW coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1, 2, and 4 is unchanged, including CameraHMR and Multi-HMR for reconstruction, BUDDI for interactions, and WHAM, TRAM, and GVHMR for world-space motion.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and 8 retain identical preprocessing, splits, training budgets, model resolutions, metrics, and evaluation controls, including removal of test-time flip augmentation from the video comparisons.

E4.justification: The box and mask prompt demonstrations, text-prompt ablation in Table 3, interaction ablation in Table 5, and supplementary interaction analysis in Section 7.1/Figure 9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and qualitative results in Figures 4–9 are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains PromptHMR-Vid's WA-MPJPE100 of 71.0 and W-MPJPE100 of 216.5.

T1.justification: Section 3 contains identical human and prompt definitions, mappings, translation parameterization, and loss formulations. No mathematical reasoning, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning flexible prompting, full-image context, reconstruction accuracy, robustness, and image/video performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain identical, including interpenetration during close interactions in Section 4.1 and the need for user-supplied shape descriptions and interaction prompts in Section 5.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, sampling rates, and prompt-generation procedures in Sections 4 and 8 are unchanged. The existing project URL is relocated, with the same destination and code/model availability statement.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 74 reference entries are identical. Positioning relative to cropped-image methods, full-image methods, language-based approaches, and interaction reconstruction remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing project URL moves from Figure 1's caption to a standalone line beneath the affiliations, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Research prose, headings, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The relocated URL shifts Figure 1 and its caption downward and reflows the abstract on page 1. Figure content is unchanged, and pages 2–15 have identical rendered appearances.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing project link more prominent and adjusts the first-page layout. Methods, experimental evidence, claims, limitations, references, and supplementary details are identical, so these cosmetic edits produce no meaningful net change in paper quality.
